run.market_summary: 1) Nvidia shock: Jensen Huang has resigned amid a scandal over chips reaching China. Congress backs tighter export curbs, the Senate wants testimony from Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick, and the White House is reportedly weighing firing Lutnick. Money is moving out of NVDA (−8.5% over 5 days) and into its competitors (AMD +45%, LRCX +26%), so chips are not falling as a group. 2) Hawkish turn at the Fed: after a hot October CPI, Fed Governor Waller floated a half-point hike, a wholesale price (PPI) report is due that could tip the Fed further, Treasuries are having their worst week since 'liberation day', and the dollar is at a 19-month high. Stocks have shrugged this off so far (SPY +3.3%, QQQ +6.4%). 3) Iran and the US are trading strikes near the Strait of Hormuz (an attack on Sirik, then an Iranian strike on a US radar in Bahrain, then IRGC threats of a harsher response). Defense stocks have already rallied but crude has not.

ideas.thesis: After a hot October CPI and Waller floating a 50bp hike, the Fed has gone from expecting cuts to fighting inflation, and Treasuries are having their worst week since 'liberation day'. Long-duration bonds should keep falling while the market prices in more hikes.

Iran says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain to retaliate for a strike on Sirik near the Strait of Hormuz, and the IRGC is threatening a 'harsher response'. Even so, USO is down 1.4% over five days, so oil is not yet pricing the risk to Hormuz supply.

The CEO has left in the middle of a scandal over chip exports to China. Congress backs tighter Nvidia export curbs and the Senate wants Huang and Lutnick to testify, so the story should keep running. Nvidia-specific selling is pushing money into its peers.

analysis.headline: Stocks opened higher after a slightly cooler-than-expected October PPI, then gave it back as the chip trade that followed Huang's exit unwound: AMD -8.8%, AVGO -4.8%, SMH -3%, and NVDA swung from +2% to -2%. Money moved into staples, financials, energy and Meta, while Bitcoin broke below $70k on hawkish-Fed and dollar pressure.
analysis.narrative:
Almost nothing in the stock or bond watchlist moved more than 1.5 standard deviations. SPY -0.38% (z -0.3), QQQ -1.2% (z -0.5), DIA +0.1%, and 8 of 13 sectors rose on below-average volume. This was a rotation inside a quiet tape, not a risk-off day. The only outsized moves were in crypto: BTC -4.2% (z -2.0) and IBIT -3.5% (z -1.5). The shape of the day matters more than its size. Index futures gapped up (SPY +0.39%) and stocks rose at first after October PPI came in at +0.3% m/m against +0.4% expected (CNBC/Yahoo live blogs). The year-on-year rate was still 6.5%, the highest since 2022. From there the session faded steadily, led by semis (SMH intraday -2.5%, XLK intraday -1.9%).

The selling was in chips. The model's "rotation within chips" story fell apart. AMD (+18.9% over 5 days), AVGO (+18.2%) and LRCX (+12.7%) had been the money-out-of-Nvidia winners, and they gave much of it back. AMD fell 8.8%, Broadcom 4.8% after a Rothschild Redburn downgrade to Neutral with a $398 target (TIKR/Seeking Alpha/Moomoo), and LRCX and AMAT about 3%. Intel, Micron, Sandisk and SK Hynix also fell. NVDA, the model's short, opened +2.2% but closed -2.0%. HSBC cut it to Hold with a $170 target, and its market cap closed below $4T. Chinese AI and hardware stocks had already slid overnight on export-curb headlines, and Lutnick agreed to testify, so the export-control story kept weighing on the group. Benzinga and Baird pinned the US selling on unwinding stretched positions and on worries about returns from AI spending, not on new policy. Cisco also fell about 6% despite its beat. The money went to names with little AI exposure. Staples led (XLP +1.4%, Benzinga "Consumer Staples Leads Sectors As Technology Trails"), followed by financials, energy and health care. Apple hit an intraday record before fading. Meta rose 2.9% on its completed €9B euro bond deal and ARK buying. MSFT gapped down on a global Outlook/Teams/Copilot outage, then recovered to close +0.2%.

Rates kept up the hawkish backdrop without adding to it. The 10-year rose 5bp to 5.15% (an intraday high near 5.17%), almost all of it before the open. Per AP, the 2-year actually slipped about 2bp after the soft PPI print, so the curve steepened. The long end still has no buyers, while the front end already prices about 87% odds of a 25bp December hike (CME FedWatch via CNBC). Bowman added that inflation has "persisted for longer than I had hoped." The dollar rose 0.27% to a 19-month high and gold slipped, consistent with hawkish policy. Bitcoin took the hit. It broke $70k for the first time since August, with a low near $67.6k, amid about $1B+ in weekly spot-ETF outflows, roughly $1.6B in liquidations and MSCI dropping MSTR from indexes. Some also cited next week's Anthropic IPO pulling in speculative money.

Iran is the dog that didn't bark. Despite the Bahrain-radar strike and IRGC threats, crude rose just 0.3%, gold fell and defense names dropped (LMT -1.3%). The IEA said the oil market is back in surplus as Russian output recovers, which offset the geopolitical risk. VIX rose only 3%, to about 20, after falling 25% over the week.

analysis.cross_asset_read: Long yields rose (10-year +5bp to 5.15%) while the 2-year slipped after the soft PPI. The dollar rose, gold fell, Bitcoin broke support and VIX barely moved (+3%). That is hawkish-rates pressure on duration and speculative assets, not broad fear. Losses were concentrated in semis and crypto, while staples, financials, energy and health care rose, so this was a rotation, not de-risking. Crude was flat and defense stocks fell despite the Iran-US strikes, so markets are not paying for that geopolitical risk, helped by the IEA's oversupply report. The yield rise came before the open while the equity fade came intraday, which means rates were not the trigger for the chip selloff. The trigger was positioning and AI-specific worries.

axis_realized.note: 10-year +5bp to 5.15%, dollar at a 19-month high, gold and Bitcoin lower; 87% odds of a December hike priced. The front end eased slightly after PPI, so the hawkish pressure was at the long end.
October PPI +0.3% m/m vs +0.4% expected (6.5% y/y). Stocks and the 2-year briefly rallied, then the effect faded.
Curb momentum (Lutnick testimony, Congress bills) hit Chinese AI stocks overnight and contributed to broad US semi weakness, though the positioning unwind was the bigger factor.

model_grade.summary: Two of three trades paid (short NVDA +2.0%, short TLT +0.4%) and the hawkish-Fed call held up. But its main chip thesis, that money rotates out of NVDA into rivals so chips don't fall together, broke badly as AMD, AVGO and LRCX fell harder than NVDA. The Iran and oil call (long USO) did nothing.
got_right: Short NVDA: -2.0% (+1.6% vs SPY), helped by the HSBC downgrade and the intraday reversal
Hawkish monetary policy and strong dollar: dollar at a 19-month high, December hike priced, gold and BTC lower
Export-control story kept running (Lutnick to testify, China protests)
got_wrong: 'Chips are not falling as a group': they did. AMD -8.8%, AVGO -4.8%, SMH -3.0%, and the rivals fell more than NVDA
Long USO: -0.34%. Iran headlines didn't move crude, and defense stocks fell
Scored geopolitical_conflict +0.50 as a major theme, but it had no visible effect on prices
Implied PPI could tip the Fed toward 50bp; the print was cooler than expected and the 2-year eased
missed: Bitcoin and crypto breakdown below $70k (the day's largest z-move), driven by ETF outflows, the hawkish Fed and MSCI's MSTR removal
Defensive rotation into staples, financials and health care, and Apple's record high on AI-light demand
IEA oil-surplus report (Russian output rebound), which offset Iran risk
Broadcom and NVDA analyst downgrades, and Meta's strength
Mean-reversion risk after +18-19% 5-day runs in AMD and AVGO

lessons: Recheck rotation trades against recent run size: when the 'winners' of a rotation are up 15%+ over 5 days, assume high reversal risk and treat a long-rival/short-NVDA pair as the only expression, not 'chips won't fall together'

Require crude to confirm before going long oil on geopolitical headlines, and check supply-side news (IEA/OPEC reports) the same morning. Three days of Iran-US strikes with flat crude should lower the geopolitical score, not raise it
Feed monetary_policy scores into crypto (BTC, IBIT, MSTR, COIN, HOOD). A strong dollar plus high real yields plus ETF outflows was the cleanest transmission of today's hawkish theme

On data days, score against consensus: with 87% of a December hike already priced, a PPI in line or slightly cool is two-sided. Watch long-end vs. front-end behavior (bear steepening) rather than assuming one 'hawkish' direction
Add a defensive-rotation leg (XLP, XLV) when the morning model flags concentrated risk in a mega-cap theme, since index-level moves stayed small while sectors split
